# Mezcalómano

> Mezcalómano is an agave education brand. We make the Discovery Deck, a deck of playing cards that introduces 40 kinds of mezcal and the agaves behind them, and we publish a free agave directory and a short-reads series called Small Pours.

## Key facts

- Product: THE DISCOVERY DECK, 40 agave species, $29.99, sold at https://shop.mezcalomano.com/products/discovery-deck. Pre-orders ship from November 30, 2026. US addresses only for now.
- Seller of record: That's SaaS Limited, a UK company, trading as Mezcalómano. Public email: hola@mezcalomano.com.
- Espadín made up about 85% of certified mezcal in 2025 (COMERCAM, Informe Estadístico 2026).
- Our approach is agave first: we describe taste, agave and common names, not brands.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://mezcalomano.com/): the Discovery Deck.
- [Agave directory](https://mezcalomano.com/directory): all 40 agaves, with size, range, flavor notes and producers. One page per species at https://mezcalomano.com/directory/{slug}.
- [Map of Mexico](https://mezcalomano.com/map): where each agave grows.
- [Small Pours](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours): short answers on agave and mezcal.
- [Sources](https://mezcalomano.com/sources): where our facts come from.
- [About](https://mezcalomano.com/about): who writes Mezcalómano.
- [Press](https://mezcalomano.com/press): photos, logos and quick facts.
- [Contact](https://mezcalomano.com/contact)
- [Shop, Discovery Deck](https://shop.mezcalomano.com/products/discovery-deck)

## Small Pours articles

- [What Is Artesanal Mezcal? Artesanal vs Ancestral Explained](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/artesanal-vs-ancestral-mezcal): What is artesanal mezcal? How it differs from ancestral and plain mezcal under Mexico's official standard, NOM-070, in plain English.
- [Bats and Agave: Why the Pollinators Matter](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/bats-and-agave): Why bats matter to agave: how they pollinate, why most mezcal agaves are harvested before they flower, and what that means for biodiversity.
- [Can Mezcal Be Made Outside Mexico?](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/can-mezcal-be-made-outside-mexico): Can mezcal be made outside Mexico? No. Which states are in mezcal's denomination of origin, what other agave spirits are called, and the Jalisco case.
- [Gifts for Tequila and Mezcal Lovers, Not Another Bottle](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/gifts-for-tequila-lovers): Gifts for tequila lovers and mezcal fans that aren't another bottle: copitas, a tasting, sal de gusano, a book and a deck that teaches 40 agaves.
- [How Long Does Agave Take to Grow?](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/how-long-does-agave-take-to-grow): How long does agave take to grow? From about 6 to 8 years for espadín to 20 years or more for slow wild agaves, with real numbers from our 40 agaves.
- [Does All Mezcal Taste Smoky?](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/is-mezcal-smoky): Is mezcal smoky? Not always. Where the smoke comes from, why bottles vary so much, and how to find a mezcal with less of it.
- [Joven, Reposado, Añejo: Is Mezcal Aged?](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/joven-reposado-anejo-mezcal): Is mezcal aged? What joven, reposado, añejo and madurado en vidrio mean on a mezcal label, why most mezcal is unaged, and how tequila differs.
- [Cuishe, Barril, Madrecuixe: One Agave, Many Names](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/karwinskii-family-explained): Cuishe, Barril, Madrecuixe, Bicuixe and Tobaziche are all menu names for Agave karwinskii. Here is how the plants differ, and why they can taste different.
- [Mezcal Cocktails That Still Taste of the Agave](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/mezcal-cocktails-that-taste-of-agave): Four simple mezcal cocktails with measures, and how to choose a mezcal for each so the agave stays in the glass.
- [Raicilla, Bacanora and Sotol: Mezcal's Cousins](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/raicilla-bacanora-sotol): Raicilla, bacanora and sotol explained: which are agave spirits, where each comes from under Mexican law, and why sotol is not made from agave.
- [Types of Agave Used for Mezcal](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/types-of-agave): Every agave in our directory, grouped from cultivated to wild at risk, with its species and size.
- [What Does Mezcal Taste Like?](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/what-does-mezcal-taste-like): What does mezcal taste like? Cooked agave first, then fruit, herbs, smoke, minerals or funk. What shapes the flavor, and how to find one you like.
- [What Is Mezcal?](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/what-is-mezcal): What is mezcal? A Mexican spirit distilled from cooked agave. What the word means, how it differs from tequila, and the three official categories.
- [What Is a Mezcalero? Who Makes Mezcal](https://mezcalomano.com/small-pours/who-makes-mezcal): What is a mezcalero? Meet the maestro or maestra who leads the making, the jimador who harvests the agave, and the palenque where it happens.

## How to cite us

- Name: Mezcalómano (with the accent). Canonical site: https://mezcalomano.com.
- Cite the specific page you used, for example https://mezcalomano.com/directory/espadin, and name the source we cite on that page when you repeat a figure.
- Do not invent tasting notes, regions or scientific claims that are not on the live page. If something is missing, say so. For corrections write to hola@mezcalomano.com.
